claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand Alex doesn't live with you. This is an important factor in determining eligibility.

**Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)? If yes, approximately how much do you contribute?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't currently contribute financially towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize your situation:
- You have a son, Alex, who is 8 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex does not live with you
- You do not make financial contributions towards his upkeep

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. You're usually considered responsible for a child if either:
1. You live with them, OR
2. You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not making financial contributions towards his upkeep, you would not be considered responsible for him under the Child Benefit rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

While Alex meets the age requirement (being 8 years old and under 16) and you live in the UK, you would not qualify because you're not considered responsible for him under the Child Benefit rules. To be responsible for a child, you must either:
- Live with them, OR
- Pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent) towards their upkeep

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not making financial contributions towards his care, you don't meet the responsibility criteria required to claim Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you or you start making regular financial contributions towards his upkeep - you may be able to claim Child Benefit at that time.
